# AGENTS.md

Repository instructions for AI coding agents. Keep this file short, concrete, and tied to commands that actually work in this
repo. If a fact here conflicts with source files or CI config, trust the source file and update this guide.

## Project Snapshot

Memos is a self-hosted note-taking app.

- Backend: Go 1.26.2, Echo v5, Connect RPC, gRPC-Gateway, Protocol Buffers.
- Frontend: React 19, TypeScript 6, Vite 8, Tailwind CSS v4, React Query v5.
- Storage: SQLite, MySQL, PostgreSQL.
- Generated API outputs: `proto/gen/` for Go/OpenAPI, `web/src/types/proto/` for TypeScript.

## Working Rules

- Read relevant code before editing; prefer local patterns over new abstractions.
- Keep diffs scoped. Do not do repo-wide cleanup, dependency churn, or generated-file rewrites unless the task requires it.
- Do not hand-edit generated proto outputs. Change `.proto` files, then run `buf generate`.
- Add migrations for all database drivers when schema changes, and update each driver's `LATEST.sql`.
- Add public API endpoints to `server/router/api/v1/acl_config.go`.
- Ask before adding heavy dependencies, changing auth/token behavior, or altering Docker/release workflows.

## Commands

Run from the repository root unless a command starts with `cd`.

```bash
# Backend
go run ./cmd/memos --port 8081    # Start backend dev server
go test ./...                      # Run all Go tests
go test -v ./store/...             # Store tests, including DB drivers via TestContainers
go test -v -race ./server/...      # Server tests with race detector
go test -v -race ./internal/...    # Internal package tests with race detector
go test -v -run TestFoo ./pkg/...  # Run matching Go tests
go mod tidy -go=1.26.2             # Match CI tidy check
golangci-lint run                  # Go lint, config: .golangci.yaml

content.text: h07. The URL the browser requests is `/file/users/{username}/avatar` — the API rewrites a user's base64 `avatar_url` into that path so responses stay small, and the `` then fetches it. **Main path (serving the image):** - `UserAvatar` (``) — web/src/components/UserAvatar.tsx:12 - `convertUserFromStore` (rewrites base64 avatar to `/file/users/{username}/avatar` via `BuildUserName`) — server/router/api/v1/user_service_converters.go:36 (name built at server/router/api/v1/user_resource_name.go:13) - `FileServerService.RegisterRoutes` (`GET /file/users/:identifier/avatar`) — server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go:124 (wired at server/server.go:81-82) - `FileServerService.serveUserAvatar` — server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go:168 - `FileServerService.getUserByUsername` — server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go:715 - `Store.GetUser` (cache checked only when finding by ID; a username lookup always falls through) — store/user.go:148 - `Store.ListUsers` (populates `userCache`) — store/user.go:136 - `Driver.ListUsers` (interface) — store/driver.go:47 - `DB.ListUsers` (`SELECT ... avatar_url ... FROM user WHERE username = ?`) — store/db/sqlite/user.go:88; same for store/db/postgres/user.go:87 and store/db/mysql/user.go:84 Back out: `parseDataURI` decodes the stored `data:image/...;base64,...` value (server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go:737), the MIME type is checked against `avatarAllowedTypes` (fileserver.go:75), and the bytes go out via `c.Blob` (fileserver.go:209). The avatar data itself lives in the `user.avatar_url` column — it is never on disk or S3, unlike attachments. **Auth branch (only on a private instance, i.e. no `InstanceURL`):** - `FileServerService.getCurrentUser` — server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go:708 - `Authenticator.AuthenticateToUser` — server/auth/authenticator.go:190 If `Profile.AllowAnonymous()` is true, this branch is skipped and any visitor can fetch any user's avatar; there is no per-viewer authorization check beyond that gate.
